original_question: For a semisimple-target equivariant map Lie algebra M and a general M-module V, describe the cohomology and homology of M in greater generality: determine H^1(M, V), understand the special case H^1(M, M_ad) related to derivations, and determine the groups H_*(M, V), including how perfectness and representation-theoretic structure are reflected in these invariants.
target_in_paper: Section 4.3.2, "Cohomology": the open problem asking for a description of H^1(M,V) for a general M-module V, the special case H^1(M,M_ad)=Der_k(M)/IDer(M), and the related problem of determining H_*(M,V) for an equivariant map Lie algebra M=M(X,g)^Γ with semisimple target g.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s actual target. It correctly identifies the semisimple-target equivariant map Lie algebra setting, the main focus on first cohomology for a general module V, the distinguished adjoint-module case tied to derivations, the related homology problem H_*(M,V), and the relevance of perfectness.
missing_details: The ambient setting should be made explicit: k is an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, X is an affine scheme with coordinate ring A=O_X(X), Γ is a finite group acting on X and on g by automorphisms, g is a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra, and M=(g⊗A)^Γ.
The paper asks for first cohomology H^1(M,V), not for a computation of all cohomology groups H^i(M,V).
The cohomology in question is Lie algebra cohomology, and the motivating equivalence is Ext^1_M(V1,V2)≅H^1(M,Hom_k(V1,V2)).
The adjoint module notation M_ad and the identity H^1(M,M_ad)=Der_k(M)/IDer(M) should be stated explicitly, including that Der_k(M) denotes k-derivations and IDer(M) inner derivations.
The related homology problem is Lie algebra homology H_*(M,V); the paper specifically singles out H_0(M,M_ad)=M/[M,M].
The role of perfectness should be made precise as the condition [M,M]=M, equivalently M/[M,M]=0.

The representation-theoretic consequence should be stated concretely: Theorem 3.2 shows that perfect equivariant map Lie algebras have a simpler classification of irreducible finite-dimensional representations.
The paper also notes a known partial result: for some equivariant map algebras, including multiloop algebras, H^1(M,V) has already been described for locally-finite M-modules.
refined_question: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, X an affine scheme with coordinate ring A=O_X(X), Γ a finite group acting on X and on a finite-dimensional semisimple Lie algebra g by automorphisms, and M=M(X,g)^Γ=(g⊗A)^Γ. Describe the Lie-algebra first cohomology H^1(M,V) for an arbitrary M-module V; in particular, determine the adjoint-case quotient H^1(M,M_ad)=Der_k(M)/IDer(M). Also determine the Lie-algebra homology groups H_*(M,V), especially H_0(M,M_ad)=M/[M,M], so as to understand when M is perfect ([M,M]=M), a condition singled out in the paper because Theorem 3.2 yields a simpler classification of irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules in that case.
justification: This is the exact open problem stated in Section 4.3.2. The paper first fixes the Lie setting M=M(X,g)^Γ with g a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0, and then in Section 4.3.2 further assumes that g is semisimple. That section explicitly asks for a description of H^1(M,V) for a general M-module V, singles out the adjoint case H^1(M,M_ad)=Der_k(M)/IDer(M), and then raises the related problem of determining H_*(M,V). The draft’s mention of perfectness is faithful, but in the paper this is tied specifically to H_0(M,M_ad)=M/[M,M] and to the fact, recorded in Theorem 3.2, that perfect equivariant map Lie algebras have a simpler finite-dimensional representation theory.
